title: ctrl + alt shortcut remat keeps on being rejected

status.label: Clarify the Ctrl+Alt shortcut warning
status.detail: The screenshots show a Ctrl+Alt mapping and a warning that some shortcuts could not be remapped, but not which mapping failed or whether continuing applies it.

judgment.rationale: The report lists PowerToys 0.94.1, says a Ctrl+Alt shortcut is repeatedly rejected, and describes using remapping to pass push-to-talk keys to non-admin VoIP apps. The supplied screenshots show a Ctrl+Alt source and destination and a dialog saying some shortcuts could not be remapped, with Continue anyway and Cancel options. They do not establish the exact intended source/target keys or whether the mapping is rejected, applied with a warning, or ineffective in the VoIP application.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.94.1 on Windows 11 with PowerToys running as administrator.
The reporter wants to rebroadcast push-to-talk shortcuts to non-admin VoIP apps such as Discord.
The configuration screenshot shows Ctrl(left)+Alt(left) source and destination fields.
The dialog screenshot says some shortcuts could not be remapped and offers Continue anyway or Cancel.
No comments or text transcribing the exact rejected key combination are present.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the exact source and target shortcuts, whether the reporter chooses Continue anyway, and what the VoIP app receives; then decide whether the warning is a real validation failure or an expected conflict notice.

fix_assessment.rationale: If a supported Ctrl+Alt push-to-talk mapping is rejected or fails to reach a non-admin VoIP app, Keyboard Manager should distinguish an advisory conflict warning from an invalid mapping and deliver the configured shortcut. The supplied screenshots do not yet establish which behavior occurs.

proposed_fixes.title: Accept supported Ctrl+Alt push-to-talk mappings
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The editor may be treating a supported Ctrl+Alt source or destination as an invalid remap, or the mapping may be accepted but not delivered across the reported elevation boundary; the current evidence does not distinguish these cases.
plan: Capture the exact source and target shortcut values and whether Continue anyway is selected.
Reproduce the mapping in Keyboard Manager 0.94.1 or current stable and observe whether it is saved, enabled, and delivered to the named non-admin VoIP application.
Determine whether the dialog represents a hard validation failure or an advisory conflict before changing validation behavior.
If a supported mapping is incorrectly rejected or not delivered, correct that specific validation or input-delivery path and add a regression test.
verification: Supported Ctrl+Alt source and target mappings are accepted and saved.
The configured push-to-talk action reaches the intended non-admin VoIP application.
Any real conflict warning clearly distinguishes continuing with the mapping from canceling it.

confidence.rationale: The screenshots show a warning dialog but not the exact key combination or the outcome after continuing, so the failure may be validation, an advisory conflict, or app/elevation behavior.

issue_context.summary: A Ctrl+Alt shortcut used for push-to-talk rebroadcasting is described as rejected; screenshots show a Ctrl+Alt mapping and a warning dialog but do not establish the exact mapping or outcome.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.94.1 on Windows 11 and says PowerToys runs as administrator.
The stated use case is to rebroadcast push-to-talk shortcuts to non-admin VoIP applications such as Discord.
The configuration screenshot shows Ctrl(left)+Alt(left) fields on both sides of the mapping.
The dialog offers Continue anyway or Cancel after saying some shortcuts could not be remapped.
inferences: The dialog may be an advisory conflict warning rather than a hard rejection, but the issue does not say whether the reporter continues or whether the mapping works.
issue_context.analysis: The screenshots are useful evidence and should not be requested again. Ask only for the exact source/target keys and the result of continuing, including what the VoIP application receives; this distinguishes editor validation from runtime delivery.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body and visually inspected both supplied screenshots.
No comments, linked fixes, or duplicate issues are identified in the report.

information_gaps.information: The exact source and target key sequences, whether Continue anyway is selected, and whether the mapping is saved and delivered to the VoIP application
information_gaps.why_needed: The screenshots show only Ctrl+Alt fields and a warning dialog; they do not show whether a third key is configured or whether the mapping fails after the warning.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the exact source and target shortcuts, say whether you choose Continue anyway, and describe whether the mapping appears saved and what the VoIP application receives.
